GTM.hook: The world's largest exporter of cardamom, a spice barely used in its own kitchens — almost the entire crop is shipped to the Middle East.
GTM.place: The first link in the Central American chain, directly south of Mexico.
GTM.borders: Spanish provincial lines from the old Captaincy General; the ruler-straight eastern edge is the 1859 Anglo-Guatemalan treaty line around British Honduras — a line Guatemala disputed so long the claim went to the world court in the 2020s.

HND.hook: The original banana republic — the phrase was coined for it in 1904, when US fruit companies effectively ran the country.
HND.place: The wide part of the isthmus, between Guatemala and Nicaragua, with a long Caribbean coast.
HND.borders: The Coco river line with Nicaragua took a 1906 royal arbitration (upheld by the world court in 1960), and the short El Salvador line was only finished by a 1992 ICJ ruling — two decades after the two fought the 'Football War'.

NIC.hook: Largest country in Central America, and its lake has bull sharks — they swim up the San Juan river from the Caribbean and stay.
NIC.place: The middle of the isthmus, between Honduras and Costa Rica.
NIC.borders: Bounded by arbitration: the Coco river line with Honduras from a 1906 award Nicaragua resisted for fifty years, and the San Juan river line with Costa Rica from an 1858 treaty still argued over navigation rights.

PAN.hook: The isthmus runs east-west, not north-south — so in Panama City the sun rises over the Pacific and sets over the Atlantic.
PAN.place: The S-bend at the bottom of Central America, joining the continent to Colombia.
PAN.borders: Was Colombia's northernmost department until 1903, when it seceded with US backing to make way for the canal — so the Colombian border is just the old provincial line through the roadless Darién jungle.

CRI.hook: Abolished its army in 1948 and put the money into schools and hospitals — it has not had one since.
CRI.place: Between Nicaragua and Panama, near the bottom of the isthmus.
CRI.borders: The 1858 Cañas–Jerez treaty put the border on the San Juan river's Costa Rican bank — Nicaragua owns the water; the Panama line dates from when Panama was still Colombia, confirmed by later arbitration.

SLV.hook: The smallest country in mainland Americas, and the only one in Central America with no Caribbean coast at all.
SLV.place: Pacific side only, wedged between Guatemala and Honduras.
SLV.borders: Old Spanish provincial lines so vaguely drawn that pockets of the Honduran border stayed contested until the International Court allocated them in 1992 — the dispute that helped spark the 1969 Football War.

BLZ.hook: The only Central American country with English as its official language, and home to the largest barrier reef in the northern hemisphere.
BLZ.place: The small notch on the Caribbean side, east of Guatemala and just below Mexico's Yucatán.
BLZ.borders: The limits of a British logging settlement: the straight western and southern lines come from the 1859 treaty with Guatemala, which later claimed the whole country — a claim both sides finally sent to the world court.
